subject: Lumenix amendment: scope reclassification & billing uplift request
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Sara Kim <contracts@lumenix.com>; Daniel Park <daniel.park@lumenix.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Lumenix amendment: scope reclassification & billing uplift request

Hi Sara / Daniel,

Thanks for taking time last week to walk through Lumenix's Q2 throughput spike and projected growth. Per our conversation, we scoped a short amendment that does two things: (1) reclassifies an existing edge-inference workload from "standard" to "dedicated burst" in Exhibit B, and (2) temporarily increases monthly committed capacity for 3 months while you finish model consolidation.

Ask: Please review the attached draft amendment and Exhibit B redline (Lumenix_Amendment_v1_redlines.pdf and Lumenix_SOW_Exhibit_B_reclass_draft.docx). High level commercial impact: +20% list rate on the reclassified workload for the 3-month uplift window; estimated sticker change is in pricing-runbook-20270402.xlsx. We recommended a phased billing approach — 50% of uplift billed upfront and 50% at ramp completion — to keep cashflow predictable for both sides.

Key constraints from our side:
- We need legal sign-off on a temporary SLA carve-out for the reclassified pool (limited SLA credit exposure).
- We cannot materially change the data retention or telemetry terms in the MSA.

Next steps I'd propose: 
1) You review the redline and flag any MSA conflicts.
2) If acceptable, we send a DocuSign packet for signatures for the amendment and updated Exhibit B.
3) Finance to confirm PO and billing contact for uplift invoice.

If you prefer, we can set up a 30-minute legal sync early next week.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this quickly.

Best,
Michael
Michael Grant
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0129

Attachments: Lumenix_Amendment_v1_redlines.pdf (redline), Lumenix_SOW_Exhibit_B_reclass_draft.docx (draft SOW), pricing-runbook-20270402.xlsx (estimate)

From: Sara Kim <contracts@lumenix.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@lumenix.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 12:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Lumenix amendment: scope reclassification & billing uplift request

Michael —

Thanks for the detailed packet. We reviewed the draft and have a few redline items (attached). High-level questions:
1) Can Redwood confirm the ephemeral SLA carve-out language will limit credit exposure to the incremental uplift only? Our legal team is concerned about a broad carve-out that could affect core MSA credits.
2) For billing, our procurement prefers a single consolidated invoice. Can we align the uplift to be invoiced on the same cadence as our current monthly invoice rather than an upfront partial invoice?
3) Please confirm the reclassification only affects the named workload in Exhibit B and does not change performance guarantees for other workloads.

I've attached our counter-redline: Lumenix_Amendment_v1_redlines.pdf (we've annotated the SLA clause and added comments on invoicing). If you can circulate a brief internal note confirming the incremental-only SLA exposure and either accept our invoicing cadence or propose a compromise, that will help us move to signature.

If easier, we can do a 20-minute call Monday morning (their counsel is available at 09:30 PT).

Cheers,
Sara
Sara Kim
Sr. Contracts Manager, Lumenix
contracts@lumenix.com

Attachment: Lumenix_Amendment_v1_redlines.pdf (external redlines)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 15:07:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Lumenix amendment: scope reclassification & billing uplift request

Michael / Laura —

Quick internal read: Sara's primary friction points are the SLA exposure and the invoicing cadence. Proposed internal approach:
- SLA: We can draft language that explicitly ties the carve-out to the incremental capacity only and caps credit liability to the uplifted pool (suggest cap = 25% of uplift value over the 3-month window). That keeps our overall MSA exposure bounded.
- Invoicing: Accepting a single consolidated invoice is OK if we convert our revenue recognition construct internally — but finance will want a short note from Lumenix confirming PO including uplift line item. Alternatively, offer a "billing memo" that invoices monthly but flags the uplift lines for their AP. That avoids large upfront cash movement while keeping our billing control.

I've attached a proposed amendment paragraph for the SLA carve-out and a clean Exhibit B draft (Lumenix_SOW_Exhibit_B_reclass_draft.docx), and a revised pricing-runbook with cap math (pricing-runbook-20270402.xlsx).

If you want, I can join the Monday call with Sara's counsel to run the legal points.

-karthik

Attachments: proposed-amendment-SLA-paragraph.txt (internal snippet), pricing-runbook-20270402.xlsx

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Sara Kim <contracts@lumenix.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@lumenix.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Lumenix amendment: scope reclassification & billing uplift request

Sara —

Appreciate the quick review and the annotated redline. Per our internal alignment (Karthik / Laura), we've made two changes:
1) SLA carve-out language now explicitly reads that credits attributable to performance shortfalls on the reclassified workload are limited to the incremental uplift for the 3-month period and capped at 25% of uplift charges across that window.
2) Invoicing: Redwood can issue a single monthly invoice that includes uplift line items flagged. We'll include a billing memo that summarizes the uplift lines so your AP has clear PO matching. We will not require an upfront 50% cash payment if Lumenix prefers consolidated invoicing.

I've uploaded the updated amendment and clean Exhibit B to Drive and started a DocuSign packet for the amendment + Exhibit B. You can review and sign here: https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=abcd1234efgh

If your counsel wants a short call to confirm the capped exposure language, Karthik is on standby for 09:30 PT today. Otherwise, if the redlines look acceptable, sign and we'll return countersigned copy the same day.

Best,
Michael

Attachments: (Drive links included). DocuSign packet started.

From: Sara Kim <contracts@lumenix.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@lumenix.com>, lumenix-finance@lumenix.com
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 16:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Lumenix amendment: scope reclassification & billing uplift request

Michael —

Thanks — we've reviewed the updated language and the cap looks acceptable to our counsel. We're going to route for sign-off internally this afternoon. A couple of operational notes from finance: please include the uplift as a line item on the monthly invoice with the PO number LN-PO-4491 referenced on the billing memo. Our AP prefers net-45 for this amendment.

Daniel will complete the DocuSign signature later today and copy finance. Once we have executed docs I'll send the PO confirmation and include the billing contact (ap.contact@lumenix.com).

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Regards,
Sara

Attachment: none
